clue.text: Expert at getting advantage out of a nice muddle

indicators.note: the word for advantage is getting, that is receiving, the scrambled letters inside it

parts.note: profit is gain or advantage

indicators.note: a muddle is a jumble, so the letters of nice are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone skilled at turning a confused situation to their own benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddle' scrambles NICE into CIEN, and 'getting' puts it inside PROFIT; 'at' and 'out of a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone proficient is skilled, an expert at the task.

clue.text: Poet's lines disturb Londoner — not on!

indicators.note: to disturb is to throw into disorder, so the letters of Londoner are jumbled once the removed pair is set aside

explanation.surface: A protest at someone upsetting a Londoner: that is just not on!
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' says the letters O and N are taken away from LONDONER; the remaining letters, 'disturbed', make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondel is a short fixed verse form of a poet, built on two rhymes with a refrain.

clue.text: Playwright who might have contributed to The Archers?

definitions.meaning: John ..., Jacobean dramatist who collaborated with Shakespeare and Beaumont

definitions.text: who might have contributed to The Archers?
definitions.meaning: a maker of arrows would have supplied archers; The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap

explanation.definitionFit: John Fletcher was a Jacobean dramatist, and an arrow-maker supplies bowmen with their shafts.

clue.text: Potty little flying-saucer?

parts.note: the target thrown for shooting is a small disc of baked earth that sails through the air like a saucer, and it is named after a bird

explanation.definitionFit: The trap-shooting target is a small fired disc, potty in being earthenware, flung through the air.

clue.text: "A livelier — twinkles in the grass" (Tennyson)

parts.words: A livelier — twinkles in the grass
parts.note: a line from Tennyson's Maud with one word gone; the missing word is a green gemstone

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the line from Tennyson's poem Maud reads 'A livelier emerald twinkles in the grass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's line likens bright green blades to a precious green gem.

clue.text: Danced a sort of square measure

parts.note: a T-square is a sort of square used in drawing
a rod is an old unit of length

explanation.surface: Someone stepped through a square dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trod a measure' is an old phrase meaning danced, which is why the definition fits.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread a measure is an archaic idiom for dancing, so stepping out a dance is treading.

clue.text: Trains cause Ted worry

indicators.note: to worry something is to shake it about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Railway trouble gives a man named Ted something to fret about.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to teach or school them.

clue.text: Its advocates would stop drinking before nine

definitions.text: Its advocates would stop drinking before nine

parts.words: Its advocates would stop drinking before nine
parts.note: reads like early closing of pubs, but describes a movement whose supporters would have everyone stop drinking altogether

explanation.definitionFit: The movement campaigning for abstinence from alcohol wanted people to give up drink entirely.

clue.text: A puzzle to shoot full of holes

definitions.meaning: to pepper with bullets until perforated like a sieve

explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a puzzling question, and to perforate something with shot is to make it like a sieve.

clue.text: In the minority it's the reverse of overtime

definitions.meaning: minority here is the legal state of being a minor, not yet adult
the opposite of over is under, and of time, a period, an age

explanation.definitionFit: A minor is too young legally, and below-plus-era is the opposite of above-plus-time.

clue.text: Horseman's event? No, but it does 'take men of iron

definitions.text: Horseman's event? No, but it does 'take men of iron

parts.words: Horseman's event? No, but it does 'take men of iron
parts.note: sounds like a trophy for a horse rider, but it is a golf competition, and golfers play with irons

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe before 'take' is a speck on the page, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The biennial Europe-versus-USA golf contest is played by golfers wielding irons.

clue.text: Note Henry VIII returned as bunkum

parts.note: B is a musical note

indicators.note: returned means the nickname is read backwards

parts.note: Henry VIII was nicknamed Bluff King Hal

explanation.surface: A message about a Tudor king sent back as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII was popularly known as 'Bluff King Hal'; HAL reversed gives LAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunkum is empty talk or nonsense, a synonym for meaningless chatter.

clue.text: Ringleader looking sheepish

parts.note: the leading ram of a flock wears a bell, so it is a leader with a ring and literally a sheep

explanation.definitionFit: The belled castrated ram leads the flock, so figuratively one who sets the trend for others.

clue.text: Hard up because of the drought?

definitions.meaning: a river shrunk by dry weather has its level fallen

explanation.definitionFit: Being broke is an idiom from stranded boats, and a drought literally drops a river's level.

clue.text: Opposes thus furnishing a sports ground for the benefit of spectators

definitions.text: thus furnishing a sports ground for the benefit of spectators
definitions.meaning: a ground fitted out ..., that is ..., for the crowd to sit in

explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to hold out against, and a ground provided with seating banks is one with stands.

clue.text: One sorrel proved awkward with the wagons

indicators.note: proving awkward suggests the letters will not stay in order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A chestnut horse proves difficult to harness to the carts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorrel' is a reddish-brown horse here, which makes the wagons scene plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a lorry is a goods truck, a modern wagon.

clue.text: Artists notice French bird, far from 22

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist; two of them
avis is the French word for a notice

explanation.walkthrough: 22 is COMMON, so 'bird, far from common' is a rare bird, the Latin phrase for something exceptional.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means a rare bird, used for any person or thing that is exceptional.

clue.text: He's relatively a very good one taking records on

parts.note: ST, saint, is a very good person
EPs are extended-play records

explanation.surface: A thoroughly good person who takes on records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's relatively' defines by family relation: a stepson is a relative by marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a male relation through marriage, a son of one's spouse.

clue.text: Brigand might turn into a royal mouthpiece

indicators.note: turning the phrase round means the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: regal means royal
a lip is part of the mouth

explanation.surface: A bandit might become a spokesman for the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses REGAL LIP as a whole to give the answer; 'might' and 'into a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit who plunders, a looter.

clue.text: Distributor of lower-class products

parts.note: lower read as one that lows, a cow, so the products are dairy goods delivered to the door

explanation.definitionFit: The roundsman delivers dairy bottles produced by cows, the creatures that low.

clue.text: West Island bonds have their legal assurances

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland
ties are bonds

explanation.surface: Bonds from a western island carry legal guarantees.
explanation.definitionFit: A warranty is a written guarantee, a legally binding assurance.

clue.text: The pike that got away, say ?

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: loose describes something that has escaped

explanation.surface: An angler's tale of the big fish that escaped.
explanation.walkthrough: LUCE is an old name for a pike, especially a full-grown one.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish name is an old word for the freshwater predator, used in heraldry.

clue.text: Where nobody trespasses at Wimbledon

parts.note: Wimbledon is famous for tennis, but here it is the open public land of that London district, where all may walk

explanation.definitionFit: Public land open to all cannot be trespassed on, and Wimbledon has a famous one.

clue.text: Pulling ploughshares perhaps-—a co-operative venture

definitions.meaning: the labour of a yoked group of oxen or horses drawing a plough

explanation.definitionFit: A yoke of oxen hauling a plough labour together, and collaboration is joint effort.

clue.text: A hot shakedown, but don't lie on it!

indicators.note: a shakedown shakes the letters about so they settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A hot makeshift bed, but advice not to lie on it.
explanation.walkthrough: A shakedown is also a makeshift bed, which explains 'lie on it'; but the definition puns: one must not lie under a sworn pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A sworn promise must not be broken by telling falsehoods, so one does not lie on it.

clue.text: One wife at a time, Jock! Go back to Miss Johnson

parts.note: mon is a Scots form of man, as a Scotsman would say it

indicators.note: go back means the word go is read backwards

parts.note: Amy Johnson, the pioneering English aviator

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is told to stick to one wife and return to Miss Johnson.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman; MON is how he says 'man'.
explanation.definitionFit: The practice of having a single spouse is the opposite of bigamy.

clue.text: How to draw 'out Felicity's heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is everything but its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Asking how to draw out a girl's true feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe before 'out' is a speck on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring forth a response from someone is to draw it out of them.

clue.text: Revolutionary exercise makes a worker 'jump

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
spring means jump

explanation.surface: A labourer's leap counts as a radical workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnastic flip onto the hands and over is a rotating, revolving exercise.
